account_error_locked: Kemlock is locked. Unlock it from the Kemlock icon in the toolbar, then try again.
account_error_noVault: Kemlock isn't set up in this browser yet.
account_error_notKemlock: This browser doesn't sync with Kemlock Server. Set that up first.
account_error_sessionEnded: Your Kemlock Server session ended. Sign in again.
account_error_network: The server can't be reached. Check the connection and try again.
account_error_rateLimited: Too many tries. Wait a moment and try again.
account_error_auth: The server didn't accept that. Check what you typed, or sign in again.
account_error_conflict: That exists already, or can't be done in the state it is in.
account_error_badRequest: The server refused that. Check the code or the address, and try again.
account_error_server: The server couldn't do that. Try again later.
account_error_proofNeeded: This change asks for a fresh code. Ask for one and type it in.
account_error_pieceMismatch: That isn't one of the pieces shown. Type one of them as it is printed.
account_error_phraseMismatch: The words the server gave aren't the ones this browser worked out. Deny this request.
account_error_noKey: The request carries no key to seal to, so it can't be approved from here.
account_error_expired: That request has run out. The other device can ask again.
account_error_changed: The contact's keys changed since you looked. Start again and compare the numbers.
account_error_badBundle: The contact's keys can't be read, or aren't signed by them. Don't confirm them.
account_error_unreadable: The key can't be opened with this account.
account_error_pieceFormat: That isn't a Recovery Kit piece.
account_error_pieceChecksum: That piece has a typo: its check doesn't match.
account_error_pieceOtherKit: Those pieces are of different kits.
account_error_pieceDuplicate: That is the same piece twice.
account_error_filesNeedPhone: This vault has notes with attached files, which a browser doesn't keep. Move it from your phone.
account_error_moveTooLate: The move is at its last step and can't be abandoned now. Let it finish.
account_error_unavailable: This browser can't do that yet.
account_error_unsupported: This version of Kemlock can't do that.
account_error_invalid: That isn't something Kemlock can do now.
account_notice_title: A device wants to sign in to Kemlock
account_notice_body: {device} is asking to sign in to your account. Open Kemlock to approve or deny it.
account_approvals_lead: A device that signs in to your account asks an open device to let it in. Compare its five words with the ones shown here, and approve only if they are the same.
account_approvals_none: No device is waiting. A request shows here when another device asks.
account_approvals_check: Check that the new device shows these same five words.
account_approvals_differ: The server's words don't match the ones worked out here. Someone may be between you and the new device: deny it.
account_approvals_nokey: This request carries no key, so it can't be approved from this browser.
account_approvals_approved: Approved. The device is signing in.
account_devices_lead: Every device signed in to your account. Signing one out ends its session and deletes its key copy.
account_devices_confirmBody: Its session ends now. It can sign in again, and a device that isn't trusted needs an approval or the password.
account_emergency_lead: Someone you trust can ask for your vault. You have the wait to refuse. Your account key is sealed to their keys, so the server can't open it.
account_emergency_emailHint: They need a Kemlock account on this server.
account_emergency_waitHint: How long you have to refuse after they ask.
account_emergency_confirmBody: Confirming seals your account key to {name}'s keys. Ask them to read out the numbers their Kemlock shows for their account, and check that they match:
account_emergency_removeBody: The grant ends for both of you, and the sealed key is deleted.
account_emergency_asked: Request sent. They have the wait to refuse.
account_emergency_released_view: It opens with this account's key, so it lets you view their vault. The server has no route that reads their items yet, so there is nothing to show from here.
account_emergency_released_takeover: It opens with this account's key. The server's part ends at releasing it, so taking over their account isn't something it offers yet.
account_emergency_releasedBad: The key was released but doesn't open with this account's key. Ask them to confirm you again.
account_recovery_lead: Three pieces, any two of which open your account without its password or another device. Keep them apart, on paper or in a safe.
account_recovery_none: This account has no Recovery Kit.
account_recovery_made: Made {date}. Any {threshold} of {shares} pieces open the account.
account_recovery_staleNote: This kit is for an older key of the account, so its pieces open nothing. Make a new one.
account_recovery_removeBody: Removing the kit makes its pieces useless. The server asks for a fresh code first.
account_recovery_once: These pieces are shown once and aren't kept anywhere. Print them or write them down before you go on.
account_recovery_sheetLead: Any two pieces open the account. Keep each in a different place.
account_recovery_typeBackHint: This shows that what you kept can be read. Only then is the kit saved on the server.
account_recovery_replaceNote: A kit exists already: replacing it makes its pieces stop working, and the server asks for a fresh code.
account_proof_hint: A code mailed to you, or a current code of your authenticator app.
account_proof_sent: A code was mailed. It works once.
account_steps_lead: A code asked for after your password. Turn on at least one, and keep the recovery code.
account_steps_totpHint: Codes from an app on your phone.
account_steps_emailHint: A code mailed to an address you choose.
account_steps_recoveryHint: Turns every method off when it is entered, and is used up.
account_steps_webVault: Security keys, YubiKeys and Duo are set up in the web vault.
account_steps_totpHow: Type this secret into your authenticator app, then enter the code it shows.
account_steps_addressHint: The address to mail codes to.
account_steps_emailOffBody: Turning it off asks for a fresh code first.
account_steps_recoveryBody: The recovery code can undo your second steps, so showing it may ask for a fresh code.
account_steps_recoveryNone: This account has no recovery code: it was never made, or it was used.
account_steps_recoveryKeep: Keep this code where only you can read it, apart from this browser.
account_move_lead: Moves the vault's entries from Vaultwarden or WebDAV into Kemlock Server, checks them, and only then lets the old store go.
account_move_wait: This can take a few minutes. You can leave this tab open.
account_move_old_closed: The Vaultwarden home was closed. Phones still on Vaultwarden are offered the move.
account_move_old_gone: The Vaultwarden home was closed already.
account_move_old_copyKept: The Vaultwarden copy stays as it is for phones that still use it. This browser syncs with Kemlock Server only.
account_move_old_fileLeft: The WebDAV file stays as it is for phones that still use it. This browser stops syncing it.
account_move_old_blocked: The Vaultwarden home was left open: it holds something that can't be moved safely. This browser syncs with Kemlock Server only.
account_move_held: You signed in to Kemlock Server, and the move waits for your say. Continue in setup, where what moves and what stays is shown.
account_move_stopped: The move stopped at: {step}. It goes on from there.
account_move_offeredVaultwarden: This vault syncs with Vaultwarden on this server. Sign in to Kemlock Server to move it.
account_move_offeredWebdav: This vault syncs with a WebDAV folder. Sign in to Kemlock Server to move it.
account_move_nothing: This vault doesn't sync with Vaultwarden or WebDAV, or it moved already. There is nothing to move.
account_move_problem_removals: The old store's last sync would remove many entries. Keep them all, or remove them.
account_move_problem_unreadable: An item on the server can't be read here.
account_move_problem_fileMissing: A note names a file this browser doesn't have.
account_move_problem_checkFailed: What was read back differs from what was sent. Try again: only what differs is sent again.
account_move_problem_newer: This move was started by a newer Kemlock. Update this extension.
account_move_problem_filesNeedPhone: This vault has notes with attached files, which a browser doesn't keep. Move it from your phone.
account_move_problem_network: The server can't be reached. Try again.
account_move_problem_auth: Signing in failed. Sign in again.
account_move_problem_server: The server couldn't do that. Try again later.
account_move_problem_signedOut: The old store's session ended. Sign in to it again, then try the move.
account_move_problem_sessionEnded: The Kemlock Server session ended. Sign in again.
account_move_problem_older: The old store holds an older copy than this browser's. Sync it first.
account_move_problem_oldStoreGone: The old store is set up no more, so the move can't go on. Abandon it, or sign in to the old store again.
account_move_problem_editedMeanwhile: The vault was edited while the old store was read. Try again.
account_move_screenTitle: Move this vault to Kemlock Server
account_move_screenLeadVaultwarden: This vault syncs with Vaultwarden on this server. Moving writes each entry to Kemlock Server and checks it before anything is let go.
account_move_screenLeadWebdav: This vault syncs with a WebDAV folder. Moving writes each entry to Kemlock Server and checks it before the folder is let go.
account_move_screenFiles: This vault's notes have {count} attached files, which a browser doesn't keep. Move it from your phone.
account_move_screenStaysVaultwarden: Nothing is deleted from Vaultwarden until the check passes. A sealed home is closed afterwards; a plain home stays for phones that use it.
account_move_screenStaysWebdav: The WebDAV file stays as it is, for phones that still use it. This browser stops syncing it.
account_move_screenResumed: An earlier move stopped part way. It goes on from there.
account_register_lead: On this server. This browser signs in to it as a device, and you approve other devices from here or from your phone.
account_register_nameHint: Shown to people who name you as a contact.
account_register_inviteHint: From the invitation link you were sent.
account_register_forgot: Nothing can recover this password. Keep it somewhere safe, and make a Recovery Kit after you sign in.
account_register_busy: Making your account. This takes a few seconds.
account_register_signupsClosed: This server isn't open to new accounts. Ask its admin for an invitation.
account_register_accountExists: That email has an account already. Go back and sign in.
account_register_registerRefused: The server refused the account. Check the email and the password.
account_kit_lead: Two of your three pieces open your account without its password or another device.
account_kit_error_kitNone: This account has no Recovery Kit.
account_kit_error_kitStale: The kit is for an older key of the account, so its pieces open nothing.
account_kit_error_kitWrong: These pieces don't open this account's kit.
account_kit_error_kitFormat: That isn't a Recovery Kit piece.
account_kit_error_kitChecksum: A piece has a typo: its check doesn't match.
account_kit_error_kitOtherKit: The pieces are of different kits.
account_kit_error_kitDuplicate: That is the same piece twice.
sync_problem_moveUnfinished: A move into Kemlock Server stopped part way, so the vault doesn't sync until it is finished or abandoned.
setup_method_recoveryCode_hint: The code from your account's security page. It turns every second step off and is used up.
